examples.text: Eine Lokalanästhesie betäubt nur den Bereich, wo die Operation stattfindet.
examples.translation: Une anesthésie locale n’endort que la zone où l’opération a lieu.

glosses: Engourdir, étourdir, obscurcir (souvent temporairement) la conscience.

examples.text: Eine sehr kleine Menge dieser Flüssigkeit genügt, um einen Menschen zu betäuben und wehrlos zu machen.
examples.translation: Une très petite quantité de ce liquide suffit à étourdir une personne et à la rendre sans défense.

examples.text: Fast zehn Jahre lang hat in dem Dorf Mazan bei Avignon ein Mann seine Frau sediert und zur Vergewaltigung angeboten. (...) Betäubt mit einem lebensgefährlich hoch dosierten Schlafmittel, ganz weg für ein paar Stunden. Wie im Koma.
examples.translation: Pendant près de dix ans, dans le village de Mazan près d'Avignon, un homme a mis sa femme sous sédatif et l’a proposée au viol. (...) Endormie avec un somnifère à haute dose qui mettait sa vie en danger, totalement absente pendant quelques heures. Comme dans le coma.

glosses: Étouffer, noyer, supprimer, empêcher de se développer.

examples.text: Viele frühere Soldaten versuchen, ihre Erinnerungen mit Alkohol zu betäuben oder versuchen, sich selbst umzubringen.
examples.translation: Beaucoup d’anciens soldats essayent de noyer leurs souvenirs dans l’alcool ou tentent de se suicider.

glosses: (für bestimmte Zeit) gegen Empfindungen, insbesondere Schmerz, teilweise oder vollständig unempfindlich machen; taub machen

examples.text: Der Zahnarzt betäubt das Zahnfleisch, bevor er operiert.
„Er ist nicht etwa gestillt, sondern er ist betäubt, so wie bei Abmagerungskuren der physische Hunger statt mit Brot mit magenberuhigenden AntiHungerPillen betäubt wird.“

translations.source_sense_description: gegen Empfindungen, insbesondere Schmerz, teilweise oder vollständig unempfindlich machen

glosses: Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.

examples.text: fingers numb with cold
legs numb from kneeling

glosses: Emotionally unable to feel or respond in a normal way.

examples.text: numb with shock; numb with boredom

[…] when we know that hundreds are rendered homeless every day, and countless thousands are killed and wounded, men and boys mowed down like a field of grain, and with as little compunction, we grow a little bit numb to human misery.
[…] seeing the dog—somehow that made me feel again. I’d been too dazed, too numb, to feel the full viciousness of it.
[…] he submitted […] as a traitor, his mind numb with vodka, submits to a firing squad.

glosses: Dumb or stupid.
Causing numbness.

examples.text:
[…] he did lap me
Even in his own garments, and gave himself,
All thin and naked to the numb cold night.

glosses: To cause to become numb (physically or emotionally).

examples.text: The dentist gave me novocaine to numb my tooth before drilling, thank goodness.
When I first heard the news, I was numbed by the shock.

The ravviſh danke of clumzie vvinter ramps / The fluent ſummers vaine: and drizling ſleete / Chilleth the vvan bleak cheek of the numd earth, / VVhilſt ſnarling guſts nibble the iuyceles leaues, / From the nak't ſhuddring branch; […]
But her main concern is the hard seating that numbs the nether regions.

glosses: To cause (a feeling) to be less intense.

examples.text: He turned to alcohol to numb his pain.
[I was] thankful for the pain, which helped to numb my terror.

glosses: To cause (the mind, faculties, etc.) to be less acute.

examples.text: […] hunger, fatigue, and despairing hopelessness had numbed his brain […]
The noise, the rush of air past our ears, was positively terrific. It actually seemed to numb the senses and make it almost impossible to take in impressions at all.
[The sofa] exhaled a breath of trapped ancient farts, barf-smell, and antiseptic, the parfum de asylum that gradually numbed my nose to all other scents on the ward.

glosses: To become numb (especially physically).

examples.text: […] after fumbling with numbing fingers for ten or fifteen minutes, he waved his hand with a gesture of despair […]
[…] once more his feet began to numb. Again he got down and stamped the circulation going, but as soon as he began to ride again they numbed.

translations.source_sense_description: gegen Empfindungen, insbesondere Schmerz, teilweise oder vollständig unempfindlich machen

glosses: To make numb, as by cold or anesthetic.

examples.text: […] the sayd Phillip […] in the same his pilgrimage was stricken with such colde, that he fell into a palsey, and was benumbed of the right side of his body.

[…] the Cold was insufferable; nor indeed was it more painful than it was surprising, to come but ten Days before out of the old Castile where the Weather was not only warm but very hot, and immediately to feel a Wind from the Pyrenean Mountains, so very keen, so severely cold, as to be intollerable, and to endanger benumbing and perishing of our Fingers and Toes.
‘My hands are so benumbed with the cold that I can scarcely handle my knife and fork.’

glosses: To deaden, dull (the mind, faculties, etc.).

examples.text:
[…] If this law
Of nature be corrupted through affection,
And that great minds, of partial indulgence
To their benumbed wills, resist the same,
There is a law in each well-order’d nation
To curb those raging appetites that are
Most disobedient and refractory.
I struggled, and trembled, and was so benumb’d with Terror, that I sunk down, not in a Fit, and yet not myself […]
Sorrowful isolation had benumbed her sense of reality, and the power of distinguishing outward and inward was continually slipping away from her.

Five nights a week, six hours a day, for the next four months—and, fortunately, never again—I made my living by exhibiting the peculiar way I am formed. The Clinic had prepared me for it, benumbing my sense of shame, and besides, I was desperate for money.

translations.source_sense_description: gegen Empfindungen, insbesondere Schmerz, teilweise oder vollständig unempfindlich machen

glosses: Rendre insensible à la douleur par l’anesthésie.

examples.text: On employait autrefois, pour anesthésier les malades, un appareil relativement compliqué.

glosses: Rendre inactif.

examples.text: Vous ne le sentez pas, vous, quand quelqu’un a la haine de soi ? Ça le conduit à devenir mort tout en étant vivant, à anesthésier les mauvais sentiments mais aussi les bons pour ne pas ressentir la nausée d’être soi.

Veste courte en cuir et cette nouvelle sorte de pantalon, d'un blanc immaculé. Souliers à talons aiguilles recouverts de paillettes, genre fantaisie, qu'on peut voir aux pieds des filles dans les bars à champagne. Cette apparition m’anesthésia.
Il y a un monde entre gommer, anesthésier, enfouir ses émotions ou les vivre seuls – et les vivre jusqu'au bout dans la présence de Dieu.
